children: Samir Arora-backed Helios Flexicap Fund cut its exposure to HDFC Bank by 6 lakh shares in August, reducing the private lender's portfolio weight to 2.59 percent from 3.5 percent, even as it made fresh bets on Coforge and PB Fintech. The fund completely exited five stocks during the month, including Dixon Technologies, BSE and Muthoot Finance, while increasing exposure to One 97 Communications, State Bank of India and Titan Company.
HDFC Bank stake cut

Helios Flexicap reduced its HDFC Bank holding to around 32 lakh shares in August from 38 lakh shares in July. The stock's weight in the portfolio consequently fell to 2.59 percent from 3.53 percent. The reduction is notable given that the fund had increased its HDFC Bank holding in June, when it bought 5.33 lakh shares and raised the stock's portfolio weight from 3.2 percent to 4 percent.

Arora had recently flagged HDFC Bank as a key area of uncertainty. Speaking to CNBC-TV18 recently, he said the stock has become “more confused” following the bank's decision to consider both internal and external candidates for the next CEO. Arora said an external candidate could make the transition more difficult as investors would need to assess a new chief executive and strategy over a longer period.

The reduction also came alongside cuts in Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel and Welspun Corp. Reliance's portfolio weight fell to around 2.1 percent from 2.9 percent, while Bharti Airtel's declined to 1.4 percent from 2.2 percent.
Coforge, PB Fintech enter portfolio

Coforge was the biggest new position added by Helios in August. The fund bought around 10.4 lakh shares, giving the IT services company a 2.37 percent weight in the portfolio. The addition comes as Arora remains selective on the IT services sector. Speaking to CNBC-TV18, he said Helios would look to add companies capable of delivering meaningful earnings growth, rather than those guiding for flat or low growth. He said IT services stocks are unlikely to see a meaningful re-rating until earnings growth improves.

The fund also bought around 3.6 lakh shares of PB Fintech, which accounted for about 0.8 percent of the portfolio. The additions came as Helios reduced its overall equity exposure to 96.9 percent from 98.5 percent, while increasing its allocation to debt and cash.
Dixon, BSE among five exits

The fund completely exited Dixon Technologies, BSE, Muthoot Finance, Lemon Tree Hotels and Aadhar Housing Finance during the month. Dixon was a sizeable position before the exit, accounting for around 2.5 percent of the portfolio in July. The fund also exited its entire BSE holding of around 2.2 lakh shares, which had represented about 1 percent of the portfolio. Its Muthoot Finance holding stood at around 2.6 lakh shares, while it held approximately 48.4 lakh shares of Lemon Tree Hotels and 5.4 lakh shares of Aadhar Housing Finance before exiting these stocks.
Paytm, SBI and Titan among key additions

Among existing holdings, One 97 Communications saw a notable increase. Helios added shares to take its holding to around 19.3 lakh shares, with the stock's portfolio weight rising to 3.79 percent from 3.1 percent.

The increase is also notable given Arora's positive view on Paytm. He has previously identified One 97 Communications as one of the stocks he remains bullish on, alongside Eternal. The fund also raised its State Bank of India holding to around 23.3 lakh shares, taking its portfolio weight to 2.83 percent.

Its Titan Company holding rose to around 4.4 lakh shares, with the allocation increasing to 2.57 percent from about 2 percent. Other notable additions included MCX, Poonawalla Fincorp, Apollo Hospitals, Bharat Electronics, Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone and Honasa Consumer.
Portfolio remains diversified

Helios Flexicap had 68 stocks in its portfolio at the end of August, with the top five holdings accounting for about 18.2 percent of the portfolio. Eternal remained the largest holding at around 4.4 percent, followed by ICICI Bank at 3.9 percent, One 97 Communications at 3.79 percent, Adani Ports at 3.31 percent and SBI at 2.83 percent.

The portfolio remained tilted towards financials, with banks accounting for 10.1 percent, followed by finance at 9.1 percent and capital markets at 9 percent. Retailing accounted for 7.6 percent, while transport and electrical equipment accounted for 4.3 percent and 3.6 percent, respectively. The fund's AUM stood at around Rs 8,748 crore at the end of August.
Fund continues to outperform benchmark

The portfolio changes come against a period of strong relative performance for Helios Flexicap. The fund delivered 7.78 percent over one year, compared with 2.83 percent for the Nifty 500 TRI. Over six months, it returned 11.64 percent, against 6.12 percent for the benchmark. Since its November 2023 inception, the scheme has generated a 17.88 percent return, compared with 11.73 percent for the Nifty 500 TRI.
The fund's equity allocation declined to 96.9 percent in August from 98.5 percent in July.

title: Helios Flexicap Fund cuts HDFC Bank stake, adds Coforge, PB Fintech in August
